report:
Volt Typhoon targets edge routers
Actors exploit unpatched VPN appliances.
They stay hidden for months using living-off-the-land tools.
Patching and credential rotation stop the known intrusion path.

Ferry operator hit by LockBit affiliates
Attackers entered through an exposed remote desktop gateway.
Files were encrypted across 40 servers within two hours.
Offline backups let the operator restore ticketing in three days.

Harbor Lights phishing kit targets payroll staff
The kit clones a payroll portal login page.
Victims receive a text message with a short link.
Multi-factor prompts are relayed to the attacker in real time.

Northwind build plugin trojanized
A maintainer account was taken over through a reused password.
Version 4.2.1 shipped a hidden credential stealer.
Teams should pin versions and rotate build secrets.

Glasshouse group abuses misconfigured cloud storage
Public buckets exposed customer invoices.
The group scans for open buckets every night.
Blocking public access settings closes the gap.

Quill spyware found in a fake document scanner app
The app asks for accessibility permissions after install.
It reads one-time codes from incoming messages.
Removing the app and resetting passwords is advised.

Ember campaign probes water utility controllers
Attackers scan for controllers with default passwords.
No physical damage has been reported.
Changing default credentials and isolating networks reduces exposure.

Saffron fraud ring uses cloned executive voices
Callers ask finance staff for urgent wire transfers.
The voice clips come from public conference talks.
A call-back rule with a known number stops the scheme.

Tidewater actors hijack stale DNS records
Dangling records pointed at retired cloud hosts.
Attackers claimed the hosts and served fake login pages.
Auditing DNS entries each quarter removes the risk.

Marlin incident traced to a departing employee
The employee copied design files to a personal drive.
Data loss alerts fired but nobody reviewed them.
A review queue for alerts would have caught it.
